topic: Lambda Init Capture for Move and Generalized Initialization
explanation: Init capture (C++14 feature, also known as generalized capture) resolves the C++11 limitation regarding move semantics into closures. It allows the creation of a new data member within the lambda's closure object, initialized by an arbitrary expression, typically using `std::move`. This makes it possible to efficiently transfer ownership of move-only types or expensive-to-copy objects into the lambda's scope, treating move capture as a specific application of a broader initialization mechanism.
practical_example: A developer using C++14 creates a thread that processes a large buffer. By using init capture (`[buffer = std::move(large_buffer)]`), they ensure the data ownership is transferred to the lambda without incurring the overhead of copying the entire buffer.
keywords: Init Capture, Generalized Capture, Lambda Move Capture
